newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bre-X says near Busang deal with partners.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says near Busang deal with partners.

text.p: Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd chief executive officer David Walsh said on Thursday the company was at an advanced stage in talks with its Indonesian partners on the Busang gold find and expected an agreement by next week.
"We are optimistic of concluding an agreement very shortly...by next week," he told Reuters in an interview in Jakarta.
"Then we will review the offer by Barrick (Gold Corp). What terms Bre-X and PT Askatindo (Karya Mineral) come to will perhaps lead to Barrick making a revised offer.
"I say perhaps, because it (agreement with Askatindo) has not been finalised yet," he said.
Walsh said the Indonesian government had given Bre-X and Barrick until February 14 to reach an agreement with their respective local partners.
He said Bre-X had set two conditions in its joint submission to the Indonesian government with Barrick outlining their agreement to jointly develop Busang.
He added that without the conditions being satisfied "the Bre-X-Barrick deal would be very tough to make it workable".
He said the conditions could not be discussed because of a confidentiality agreement between Bre-X and Barrick.
Bre-X estimates there are at least 57 million ounces of gold currently worth over $21 billion in the Busang property in rolling hills and rain forest in East Kalimantan province on Borneo Island.
"The onus is on Barrick (to satisfy the conditions)," he said. "Perhaps the Indonesian government can take a more active role if Barrick cannot come to terms with Bre-X and its local partners."
Walsh also said there was a possibility Bre-X would not be able to reach an agreement with Barrick before the February 14 deadline set by the Indonesian government.
"There is a possibility," he said.
"I cannot answer that question at this time," he said when asked if he was confident of doing a deal with Barrick. "There's a possibility a deal with Barrick cannot be done before February 14."
Walsh also said Bre-X was in favour of providing Indonesian interests a bigger stake in Busang.
"When all this is resolved, the Indonesian interests will have a stake greater than 20 percent. This is being worked out now," he said.
Walsh said Bre-X's local partners were being represented by influential Indonesian businessman Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, a close associate of President Suharto.

He said Hasan, through the Nusamba group, had taken a 50 percent stake in PT Askatindo and a 50-percent stake in PT Amsya Lyna. The remaining 50 percent stakes in both companies are controlled by the family of Indonesian businessman Syakerani.
The Nusamba group is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto each own 10 percent.
Walsh said PT Askatindo has a 10-percent stake in Busang II and PT Amsya Lyna a 10-percent stake in Busang III.
He said Bre-X's 22.5 percent stake in the Busang property would not be watered down by its Indonesian partners.
"It's not going to be any less than 22.5 percent," he said. "It's not going to go down."

Walsh also said he wished to see a limited international bidding for the Busang property. "There should only be a few select companies we are able to negotiate with, subject to approval from our local partners and government wishes," he said.
-- K.T. Arasu, Jakarta newsroom + 6221 384-6364
